author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Once a forgotten Victorian gem in Noe Valley, this home was purchased at $1.85 million and thoughtfully revived, blending its charming historic features with modern amenities. Now boasting a listing price of $5.595 million, it offers five spacious bedrooms alongside a private apartment. The extensive restoration preserved its Victorian allure while ensuring necessary structural and aesthetic updates, reflecting the growing trend of revitalizing historic homes in sought-after urban areas.
title: SF couple's $1.85m Victorian renovation now listed for $5.595m

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: A recent ruling by an Alabama appeals court has partially overturned a juvenile court's ruling regarding parental rights. The mother has maintained her rights to her older child but lost her rights to her younger daughter. The court underscored the necessity of evaluating the circumstances of each child individually in such matters. Meanwhile, the father's rights to both children remain revoked due to evidence of substance abuse and inadequate support.
title: Court reverses loss of Alabama mother's parental rights for one of two kids

author: RAJ SHEKHAR JHA
description: Lalit Modi has announced his acquisition of British citizenship during an event at Oxford Union. While he claims to have faced threats and political persecution, he has refused to return to India. The Enforcement Directorate has ongoing investigations regarding his alleged financial misconduct linked to IPL. Previous requests for his deportation have been denied by the UK government.
title: Lalit Modi gets British citizenship, extradition prospects take a hit

author: SURENDRA SINGH
description: Three Indian contenders, including Tata Advanced Systems Ltd, submitted bids for the Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft programme. The Defence Ministry's committee is evaluating proposals for developing five prototypes based on designs by Aeronautical Development Agency. The prototypes are anticipated to undergo 1,800 test sorties to validate various performance characteristics over seven years. The aircraft aims to strengthen the Indian Air Force's capabilities as it faces a fighter squadron shortfall.
title: India’s 5th-gen stealth AMCA aircraft: 3 consortium submit bids, evaluation under way

author: DHANANJAY.MAHAPATRA
description: The Election Commission has committed to include every eligible citizen in the electoral rolls during the current process. No legal action will be taken against individuals for re-registering to vote through Form 6. Voters are advised to ensure their names are not listed in other constituencies before applying. Additionally, those previously removed erroneously can submit fresh forms for their names to be reinstated.
title: Those using Form 6 to re-enroll won't be prosecuted: EC to SC

author: TOI WORLD DESK
title: Alabama student leads UNICEF fundraising among 600 schools, raises $5,500

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: After sending threatening emails to his ex-wife, an Alabama father grappled with custody issues. The court granted sole custody to the mother, citing the father's harassment. Although the appeals court upheld this decision, they recognized that the father's visitation hours were excessively limited. Consequently, a reassessment of the visitation schedule was ordered, while a protection order against him remains active until March 2027.
title: Court backs order over dad's fake-name emails, revisits visitation limits

author: DIPAK K DASH
description: An empty Vande Bharat train journeyed 463 kilometers from Hatia to Deen Dayal Upadhyaya station despite brake problems. Two loco pilots had reported issues with the power brake before the journey commenced. An investigation revealed that brakes on every coach had been isolated, leading to joint brake failure. The South Eastern Railway's document indicated staff negligence in integrating the braking systems.
title: Empty Vande Bharat allowed to run 463km despite 'poor power brake'

title: In a first, CRPF battalion in anti-Naxal ops diverted to Manipur

author: ALIM SHAIKH
title: 'Defaming India at global platforms': Amit Shah hits back at Rahul Gandhi

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: In an exclusive edition of Country Life magazine, Prince George displayed his artistic skills with a thoughtful drawing of a kingfisher. This special issue, guided by his father Prince William, emphasizes issues such as environmental awareness and family life. Through this public piece, George connects to the creative spirit of his mother, Kate Middleton, and his grandfather, King Charles III, promoting the royal family's dedication to nature and social engagement.
title: Prince George's kingfisher drawing debuts in William's 300-page issue

author: SURENDRA SINGH
title: In a world first, China’s 10-tonne electric commercial aircraft makes crewed flight

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: A Pennsylvania appeals court has upheld a three-year protection order barring a father from contacting his former partner and their seven-year-old son. The mother alleged that he pushed his way into her home during a custody handoff, behaved aggressively and frightened the child, who later begged her not to send him with his father again.
title: Court backs 3-year order barring father from mother and 7-year-old

author: ANUJA JAISWAL
description: Out-Of-Pocket Expense Dips But Families Still Paid 4L Cr In 2023-24
title: Govt healthcare spend up 3x since 2013-14 to 4.1 lakh crore

author: DIPAK K DASH
description: A recent analysis highlights a troubling trend where many eligible hit-and-run victims fail to receive compensation. Annually, about 70,000 hit-and-run incidents occur, leading to numerous injuries and fatalities. Despite the launch of a compensation initiative in February 2022, only a limited number of claims have been successful. Victims often lack awareness of the program due to its complexity.
title: 75% of hit-and-run victims miss out on compensation: Report

author: KARAN MANRAL
title: 'Everyone influential loves Jenson': Huang discusses comeback as Nvidia CEO with allies

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
description: A study in Udawalawe National Park indicates that dwindling elephant groups result in significant social vulnerabilities. With fewer individuals, elephants transition from larger communities to smaller, more isolated factions, which impairs their capacity to nurture and feed effectively. Once a critical social threshold is exceeded, the difficulty of reversing such fragmentation intensifies.
title: Study of 440 female elephants finds social ties fray after population losses

author: NASEER GANAI
description: Kashmiri filmmakers are advocating for a shift towards regional cinema to enhance authentic storytelling and representation. They argue that Bollywood often reinforces stereotypes that misrepresent life in J&K. The current film policy is criticized for not adequately supporting local productions while favoring external filmmakers. Actors and directors are calling for collaboration among regional artists to develop a unique Kashmiri film industry, signaling a significant movement towards self-identity and cultural expression.
title: Kashmir film fraternity trains guns on Bollywood’s ‘AK-47 & skullcap’ stereotype

author: SRINIVAS LAXMAN
description: Mumbai recently held an online event to honor the birth centenary of Nobel laureate Abdus Salam. Eminent scientist Pervez Amirali Hoodbhoy delivered a lecture discussing Salam's contributions to physics and his life. Hoodbhoy highlighted Salam's significance as a symbol of goodwill between India and Pakistan. He mentioned Salam's lack of recognition in Pakistan due to his Ahmadiyya sect affiliation, affecting youth role models.
title: Mumbai physics forum hosts online lecture by Pakistani nuclear scientist

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Demi Dominguez tragically lost her life shortly after hospital discharge, following alarming preeclampsia symptoms. Her baby son, Malakhi De Leon, passed away soon after birth. A jury subsequently awarded $9.25 million in damages, yet limitations under California's MICRA restrict non-economic compensation. This heart-wrenching case underscores the urgent necessity for reform in medical negligence laws, as the families advocate for changes to protect others from similar tragedies.
title: California mother, baby died after discharge; $9.25m jury award capped

author: NASEER GANAI
description: In Jammu and Kashmir, Congress has called for a thorough investigation into the tragic killing of two special police officers. Initial reports indicate that the officers may have been accidentally shot by Army personnel during a hunting operation. The BJP has dismissed these allegations, claiming they tarnish the integrity of the security forces.
title: Cong suggests Army ‘friendly fire’ behind deaths of 2 SPOs in Kishtwar, BJP hits back

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: After hiring estate agent Rick Walters to sell his home, Jason Wagner later bought a property from him. Wagner alleges he was coerced into paying an extra $85,000 above their original agreement. The Kentucky Court of Appeals reinstated many of Wagner's claims against Walters and Lenihan Real Estate, allowing him to proceed in a lower court after previous dismissals. The decision emphasized concerns regarding Walters' financial transactions during the sale.
title: Kentucky man buys agent's $300,000 home, court revives claims over $85,000 demand

author: KANCHAN YADAV
title: 'They need dramatic shakeup': Bessent urges Nvidia to look outside firm for new CEO

author: PRISHA PATNAIK
title: 'Blockade is suffocating us': Cubans use Havana marathon to protest US sanctions

author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
description: A breeding facility in Jenera, Ohio, was revealed to have hundreds of chinchillas in poor conditions. Federal inspections led to the discovery of severe neglect and health issues in the animals. Humane World for Animals assisted in the rescue of 951 chinchillas, which were removed in two operations. The facility's owner agreed to surrender the animals and cease operations regulated by the Animal Welfare Act.
title: 951 chinchillas rescued from Ohio breeder as facility is forced to close

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: In South Dakota, a ranching family has harnessed the power of rotational grazing and cutting-edge virtual fencing to rejuvenate their land's biodiversity. By allowing grasslands to rest between grazing sessions, they have significantly improved plant health and restored native ecology. This approach not only boosts wildlife populations, such as diverse bird species and larger mammals, but also streamlines cattle management with reduced labor.
title: South Dakota ranch sees wildlife rebound after decade of grazing changes

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: A team of researchers has thoroughly examined a distorted silver sixpence from 1834, uncovering unexpected manufacturing flaws. Through intricate 3D imaging, they revealed significant deformations and patterns that stray from regular wear. This peculiar state of the coin prompts a deeper look into the production methods of the steam-powered minting period. The analysis, combining advanced imaging and chemistry, sheds light on historical minting defects.
title: £8 coin bought at car boot sale may hide 192-year-old minting error

author: PRISHA PATNAIK
title: Kishtwar SPOs killings: BJP says Congress remarks could fuel Pakistan propaganda

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: A Pennsylvania court has upheld the dismissal of Jacob Singer's case over alleged mismanagement of a family trust holding around 65 properties. It found that his claim of missing millions lacked sufficient financial evidence and that he had not established a right to an accounting or immediate control of the properties.
title: Court dismisses son's lawsuit over family trust holding 65 properties

author: KANCHAN YADAV
title: Kishtwar BJP leader questions Shagun Parihar’s mosque claim, Muslim body seeks public apology

author: HIJAM RAJU SINGH
description: Kagiso Rabada reached a remarkable career milestone by exceeding Allan Donald's wicket record, bagging five wickets to elevate his total to 606 in international cricket. Although Bangladesh faced an early struggle, they mounted a strong comeback driven by an incredible 206-run partnership between Towhid Hridoy and Litton Das, concluding the day at 327 for 6 and revitalising their innings.
title: Record alert! Kagiso Rabada surpasses Allan Donald in SA’s all-time wicket tally

author: ANJALI SINGH
description: A devastating road mishap took place on Sunday evening near Theh Kalandar village in Fazilka district, claiming the lives of five people, including three young ones. The victims were on their way home from a wedding when tragedy struck. Additionally, eleven others sustained injuries; two of them are in critical condition and were transferred to other medical facilities. Quick-thinking locals rushed to help free the trapped individuals before ambulances arrived.
title: 5 killed, 11 injured as car collides with pickup in Punjab

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: The historic Union Street School in Leesburg, Virginia has reopened as a museum and community centre. After a refurbishment costing around $6.2 million, the building now serves to educate about Black history. Initially established in 1884, it provided education to Black children during segregation until 1958. The new museum aims to preserve memories and share the stories of those associated with the school.
title: 1884 Virginia school for Black children reopens as museum after $6.2m revamp

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: David Park has successfully conserved 1,228 acres of land at Desert Creek Ranch in Nevada. This effort focuses on protecting habitats for the rare Bi-State sage-grouse while allowing continued agricultural activities. A permanent conservation agreement prevents non-agricultural development and preserves the land's ecological value. Additionally, a future grant will facilitate restoration work across 350 acres to control invasive grass and support biodiversity.
title: Nevada rancher's 1,228 acres conserved; grant to treat 350 acres

author: HIJAM RAJU SINGH
description: Gunjan, taking inspiration from Neeraj Chopra, has made history by clinching a gold medal at the Youth Olympic Games. She dominated the women's 48kg category with a decisive 5-0 victory over Algeria's Bouthaina Bensalah. This monumental achievement, alongside L Ambekar Meetei's win, signals India's first double gold in boxing at this event.
title: From Neeraj’s Olympic triumph to her own historic gold! How Gunjan found boxing

author: TOI BUSINESS DESK
description: According to the I-T department’s ‘Insight Portal’, the woman purchased an immovable property worth Rs 1.4 crore during the financial year that ended on March 31, 2016.  The portal monitors high-value financial transactions to help detect instances of tax non-payment. The case was about Section 69 of the Income Tax Act, 1961, which deals with unexplained investments.
title: Husband remits Rs 80L to seller for wife's property, she gets notice; what ITAT said

author: TOI BUSINESS DESK
description: Industry experts estimate over 1 lakh jobs in the next three years through the country’s efforts to build a semiconductor ecosystem of its own. Professionals with specialised skills, including process engineering, chip fabrication, chip design, systems engineering and product architecture, can earn four to six times the salaries of IT services professionals with similar experience. The difference is particularly pronounced at the mid-to-senior levels.
title: Semiconductor boom may add 1 lakh jobs; senior engineers earn 6x IT salar

author: ARYAN SINGH
description: During a recent event in Jodhpur, RSS leader Mohan Bhagwat spoke fervently about the necessity of national unity. He indicated that smaller identities can lead to societal rifts, reminiscent of colonial tactics. Emphasizing the need for individuals to set aside ego and self-interest, he illustrated his points with lessons from the Mahabharata, stressing that unity is key to overcoming challenges.
title: 'Divide-and-rule tactics': RSS chief Bhagwat's warning over attempts to split India

author: PRANAV SHUKLA
description: Yash Thakur made his ODI debut against New Zealand but was dismissed for a duck on Sunday. He joined the list of 18 Indian players who have scored ducks in their debut matches. While India struggled with bat early on, they managed to secure a 22-run victory in the fifth ODI. The win allowed India to clinch the series 3-1 following New Zealand's consecutive home series victories.
title: Yash Thakur joins Sachin, Dhoni in unwanted list after ODI debut against NZ

author: AASHISH VASHISTHA
title: Prince William, Kate to meet PM Modi in Delhi during three-day India visit

author: AASTHA JHA
description: The Bharatiya Janata Party's Uttar Pradesh unit has refuted claims regarding a supposed list of 209 candidates. Officials described these reports as false and part of a larger scheme. They cautioned party members against believing in unverified media stories. Additionally, they clarified that the assembly election candidate selection process has yet to commence, highlighting the importance of a methodical and unified approach to such decisions.
title: 'Well-planned conspiracy': BJP refutes reports of 209-candidate list for UP elections

author: VRITI JAIN
description: Despite facing threats and considerable opposition, Diljit Dosanjh took the stage in Indore to celebrate culture with his loyal fans. His performance included powerful couplets that highlighted resilience and strength, emphasizing that nothing would deter them from their cherished traditions. Although some emails threatened bomb blasts, authorities later confirmed them as hoaxes. Dosanjh's unwavering dedication showcased his commitment to his audience amidst adversity.
title: 'Kisi ke baap ka Hindustan thodi hai’: Diljit Dosanjh takes stage despite threats

title: From battlefield drones to bigger guns: China upgrades Pakistan-used VT-4 tank

author: ANJALI SINGH
description: In a tragic incident in Bhopal, 25-year-old journalist Sapna Kumari lost her life after falling from a bike taxi. A motorcycle swerved unexpectedly, causing her to tumble, and a dumper truck following closely ran over her. Both the motorcycle riders and the dumper driver fled the scene promptly. Authorities are now examining CCTV footage to track down those accountable for this heartbreaking accident.
title: Journalist falls off bike taxi, crushed to death by speeding dumper in Bhopal

author: ARYAN SINGH
description: The USS Spruance has made its way back to Naval Base San Diego after an unprecedented 357-day overseas deployment, the longest for an American destroyer since World War II. Amidst the escalating tensions in the US-Iran conflict, the Navy had to divert two destroyers to the Middle East, further stretching resources. Admiral Daryl Caudle emphasized the ongoing deployment crisis, revealing the strain on maintenance and future operational readiness.
title: US destroyer returns after 357 days at sea, longest since WWII

author: PRISHA PATNAIK
title: Trump blames Biden for aviation chaos, presses Congress for ATC funding

author: AASTHA JHA
title: Pakistan orders 1 lakh Turkish FPV drones, expands unmanned warfare arsenal

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
description: Recent archaeological discoveries in Beijing have unearthed remnants of the Great Wall from the Sui Dynasty, revolutionizing our understanding of its historical context. This find emphasizes the wall's role as a military outpost on the northern frontier. Additionally, three ancient wooden boats, dating back approximately 1,800 years, were recovered in Fengtai district, showcasing an early transport network in Beijing and shedding light on the area's trade and defense roles.
title: 1,400-year-old Great Wall remains and ancient boats unearthed in Beijing

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
description: The Spains Hall Estate in Essex has welcomed the return of beavers, leading to remarkable improvements in the local ecosystem. A year after their reintroduction, studies revealed an increase in both the quantity and diversity of terrestrial invertebrates. Additionally, water quality enhancements were noted, with elevated oxygen levels and diminished nitrate concentrations.
title: Beavers' return to England improves water quality and boosts wildlife in a year

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: On November 10, the Regional Food Bank of Oklahoma marked a historic milestone by packaging its one billionth meal, a testament to 46 years of tireless support from community partners and volunteers. The Oklahoma City Thunder made a significant donation to amplify hunger relief efforts. However, food insecurity still poses a critical challenge in Oklahoma, particularly affecting children.
title: Oklahoma food bank serves billionth meal; Thunder donates $25,000

author: PRANAV SHUKLA
description: Mohit Ulva expressed his thoughts on India's exhilarating win over Pakistan in the Asia Cup final. He noted that the team's celebrations were filled with joy, not aimed at inciting any reactions. Amidst social media backlash, the players concentrated solely on their pursuit, heroically chasing down 338 runs at the last moment. He highlighted the unwavering confidence in the team's spirit, even after facing the loss of eight wickets.
title: 'We did likewise': Mohit Ulva reveals why India celebrated aggressively vs Pakistan

author: AASHISH VASHISTHA
title: Trump slams judge’s order blocking Washington golf course renovation

author: ARYAN SINGH
description: In a bold statement, Suvendu Adhikari, the Chief Minister of West Bengal, sent a clear message to those involved in crime after a police encounter resulted in the death of Ratan Sheikh, a prime suspect who reportedly shot at officers during his attempted arrest. Adhikari reaffirmed that criminal activities will not be tolerated in the state. Meanwhile, the police constable injured in the incident remains in stable condition.
title: 'No place for goons': Adhikari's message after Ratan Sheikh encounter

author: HIJAM RAJU SINGH
description: Lakshya Raichandani commended Aaryavir Sehwag for his exceptional play during the Under-19 Asia Cup. Sehwag's impressive scoring led the team to triumph, showcasing a remarkable recovery following a previous defeat to Pakistan. Raichandani emphasised the critical role of a reliable batter in successful run chases, underscoring the team's resilience and the valuable lessons they learned from their earlier misstep.
title: ‘He takes pressure off’: Lakshya on Sehwag’s impact in India’s Asia Cup triumph

author: VRITI JAIN
description: A CCTV footage captured the final moments of an 18-year-old girl named Shabnam at a clothing showroom. She was allegedly attacked by a 29-year-old man named Suraj, who subsequently dragged her into a trial room. Police discovered Shabnam's body later that evening with injury marks and a knife nearby. Initial investigations suggest a fallout from their prior friendly relationship could be the motive.
title: Delhi showroom murder: CCTV shows victim's final struggle with 'ex-friend'

author: TOI CITY DESK
description: Three outsourced forest personnel were dismissed after a video showed them chasing a lion on a motorcycle. The incident occurred at Ambardi Safari Park during the Diwali festival holiday period. According to officials, the lion was being directed back to its enclosure when it strayed. An inquiry was launched, but no harassment was confirmed regarding the lion's treatment.
title: Watch: Forest staff chase lion on motorcycles at Gujarat safari park

author: VRITI JAIN
description: Mumbai Traffic Police have announced diversions, road closures and parking restrictions across south Mumbai from November 16 to 19 ahead of the visit of Prince William and Catherine, Princess of Wales, for the Earthshot Prize Summit and Awards Night. N Morarji Road will be closed to general traffic on Monday, and pay-and-park facilities are suspended on key roads.
title: Prince William, Catherine's Mumbai visit: Road closures, diversions from Nov 16-19

author: ARYAN SINGH
description: Lieutenant Colonel Brandon Carroll Tyner has been arrested in Britain on suspicion of espionage linked to Russia. The investigation is being conducted by London’s Counter Terrorism Policing and involves the FBI. Tyner was allegedly caught in an undercover sting operation while trying to assist Russian intelligence. Concerns over insider threats in NATO’s military command structure have been raised following this incident.
title: US Army names officer held in UK over suspected Russian espionage at Nato base

author: TANUJ LAKHINA
description: PT Usha's re-election bid as IOA president received a boost after Electoral Officer Sanjay K Srivastava rejected all objections to her nomination through the Ice Hockey Association of India. She features in the 71-member final electoral college, making her eligible to contest the December 5 elections after missing out on an elected Sportsperson of Outstanding Merit (SOMs) position.
title: PT Usha clears NSF eligibility hurdle; 71 members set for IOA Elections

author: PRANAV SHUKLA
description: Joe Root achieved a significant milestone by scoring his 50th ODI half-century against Australia. He contributed 62 runs to England's total of 355 runs at Adelaide. This performance helped England secure a 135-run victory and level the series at 1-1. Root's achievement places him among the elite group of ODI cricketers with numerous half-centuries. The ODI World Cup in 2027 adds importance to the upcoming decider in Hobart.
title: Joe Root scripts history vs Australia, achieves first-ever feat for England in ODIs

author: AASHISH VASHISTHA
title: NYPD shoots kidnapping suspect dead after van chase on busy highway; no child found

author: TOI BUSINESS DESK
description: Gold price outlook: Market participants will watch inflation data from India, the US, the UK, the Eurozone and Japan. The minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee meeting, remarks by Federal Reserve officials and US employment figures will also be closely monitored. Gold and silver both recorded sharp losses on the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX) over the past week.
title: Gold falls to Rs 1.36 lakh, silver down 5% on MCX this week; what’s the outlook?

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
description: In a remarkable conservation effort, 62 San Francisco garter snakes, previously raised in a zoo, have been successfully released into their natural environment. This project stems from the need to ensure the species’ survival, as they were originally taken from the wild. Alongside this, restoration activities are being implemented to enhance their habitat.
title: 62 endangered San Francisco garter snakes released into wild after zoo care

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: At just 14 years old, Chris Qian founded ReTech for Kids, a nonprofit dedicated to bridging the technology gap for students lacking access to digital tools. By refurbishing and distributing second-hand devices, the initiative has empowered under-resourced learners. Over three years, it has engaged more than 100 volunteers and provided 2,000 devices, earning Chris both accolades and the prestigious Diana Award for his extraordinary efforts towards educational equity.
title: Virginia teen helps distribute 2,000 devices, wins 2026 Diana Award

author: ARYAN SINGH
description: Akhilesh Yadav emphasized the importance of the Dalit community in upcoming Uttar Pradesh elections. He called for the ousting of the BJP government, highlighting the need for social justice. Akhilesh criticized the ruling party's record on Dalit issues, which includes the vandalism of Dr. BR Ambedkar's statues. He promised that a Samajwadi Party government would prioritize rights and education for marginalized communities.
title: Akhilesh calls Dalits 'damdar', vows to wipe out BJP in UP

author: TOI SPORTS DESK
description: The ICC has unveiled an extensive calendar for significant men's cricket tournaments spanning until 2035, which details the qualification processes. This plan features the 2027 ODI World Cup and the upcoming Men's and Women's T20 World Cups in 2028. Additionally, the qualification structure for the men's cricket events at the 2028 Olympics has been established, with eight teams vying for the final spots.
title: ICC finalises calendar till 2035: India to host 2029 Champions Trophy, co-host 2031 WC

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: In a significant ruling, the Missouri Court of Appeals reinforced a jury's verdict against therapist Craig Politte for professional misconduct, confirming charges of medical negligence, battery, and breaches of the Missouri Merchandising Practices Act. Although the jury's compensation award exceeds $2 million, punitive damages were annulled due to distinctions concerning negligence per se claims.
title: Therapist's affair with client leads to $2.1m verdict; court voids $1m

author: GEORGE MENDONCA
description: In a harrowing incident, 61-year-old chauffeur Suresh Salve was attacked and robbed in Nerul on November 9, losing Rs 1,000 and his mobile phone. After suffering serious injuries, he was taken to Terna Hospital but tragically died three days later. The police swiftly apprehended the three attackers, charging them with murder and recovering the stolen belongings shortly thereafter.
title: 61-year-old chauffeur dies after robbery in Navi Mumbai; 2 minors among 3 arrested

author: PRISHA PATNAIK
title: Punjab Congress sets up panel to vet leaders joining from other parties

author: TOI CITY DESK
description: Ratan Sheikh, a history-sheeter, was killed during a shootout with police while evading arrest. He had previously shot a constable, injuring him during the arrest attempt. This incident marks the fifth police encounter since the BJP took power in West Bengal. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari emphasized that criminals have no place in the state. The police reacted firmly to Sheikh's aggressive attempt to evade capture, following established protocols.
title: 5th encounter since BJP came to power in West Bengal: Man accused of firing at cop killed

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: Darrell Dai, a robotics research engineer at Nvidia, has resigned amid communication issues following Jensen Huang's departure. He expressed his admiration for Huang’s vision and the engineering culture he fostered. Dai felt that employees were not heard regarding decisions impacting the company's future direction. His resignation reflects a significant concern over the current leadership and its impact on employee trust.
title: 'Didn't seek our views on Jensen Huang': Nvidia research engineer resigns

author: PRISHA PATNAIK
description: Pakistan is considering expanding its administrative framework by increasing its provinces from four to twelve, aiming for more efficient governance. Senior officials argue that smaller provinces could enhance public service delivery. Yet, this ambitious initiative faces political hurdles and requires unity among major parties. Redefining boundaries will necessitate constitutional amendments, and a potential referendum may follow, pending parliamentary consent.
title: Redrawing Pak: Ministers back 12-province plan but pol, constitutional hurdles remain

author: PRISHA PATNAIK
title: Farage says Britain faces 'defencelessness', singles out Russia as top threat

author: VRITI JAIN
description: The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation will begin train services at 4.30 am on Monday, two hours earlier than usual, to help devotees travelling for Usha Arghya during Chhath Puja. Trains will start simultaneously from all terminal stations and run at 15-minute intervals until regular revenue services begin, after which the day’s scheduled timetable will apply.
title: Delhi Metro to start services at 4.30 am tomorrow for Chhath Puja Usha Arghya

author: PRANAV SHUKLA
description: Mohammad Yousuf voiced his disapproval of the Indian Under-19 team's exuberant celebrations following their nail-biting victory over Pakistan. He emphasized the need for young athletes to embody their values and upbringing, advocating for respect during competition. His remarks arose after a thrilling match where India triumphed by just one wicket, igniting a vital discussion on sportsmanship and the conduct of players.
title: 'You represent your upbringing': Mohammad Yousuf lectures India's U-19 team

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
description: In an exciting development, researchers have pinpointed potential hotspots for fossil discoveries that remain undocumented. Focusing on the Cenozoic Era, celebrated for its rich marine biodiversity, this study seeks to enhance fossil hunting by concentrating efforts on less explored territories. Additionally, revisiting collections from natural history museums could yield new insights into ancient species, reinforcing the pursuit of understanding marine life from the past.
title: Scientists map ancient sea-life fossils, find richer sites in younger rocks

author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
description: Navigating tiled floors can turn into a playful game as one finds themselves stepping on alternate tiles. This quirky behavior not only injects fun into mundane walks but also highlights how visual patterns shape our walking experiences. While many enjoy this harmless ritual, it's important to recognize when such a habit might signal deeper anxieties rather than mere amusement.
title: Psychology says stepping on alternate floor tiles may be a pattern game

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: In a significant political shift, British Columbia has ushered in a Conservative majority government after a decade dominated by the New Democratic Party. Winning 64 out of 93 seats, the Conservatives plan to place a strong emphasis on expanding liquefied natural gas production to enhance energy policy. However, they face fiscal constraints with potential deficits looming, and the new government will need to balance economic growth with public service demands.
title: BC Conservatives win power for first time since 1928 with 64 seats

author: JYOTIRMOY HALDER
description: India captain Shreyas Iyer called the New Zealand ODI series a bowlers’ contest, praising his team's resilience after a heavy fourth-match defeat. He described leadership as challenging yet exciting, backed his seamers' partnerships and said India quickly moved on from Matt Henry's devastating spell. India won the fifth ODI by 22 runs, sealing the series 3-1.
title: 'It was a series for bowlers, not batters': Iyer after India's 3-1 ODIs win over NZ

title: Turkish man sentenced to life for pushing pregnant wife off cliff freed after 6 years

author: AMAN XESS
description: An 85-year-old man sent over $1 million to a woman claiming she needed it for taxes and legal fees. Maria Auxiliadora Rezende allegedly fabricated a story concerning inherited farmland in Brazil. Family members noticed unusual transactions and investigated the situation after voicing concerns. Authorities arrested Rezende and she faces a federal indictment for wire fraud.

Police recovered evidence, including a blood-stained knife, during their investigation.

Bangladesh are still searching for their first Test win against South Africa.

description: In a strategic shift, Ukraine is turning to HiSky's advanced satellite communication terminals to enhance the operational capabilities of its long-range drones. This move seeks to mitigate reliance on SpaceX's Starlink, which faced service interruptions affecting vital military activities. HiSky's SmartLITE system offers multiple satellite network connections, ensuring robust communication for drone operations, reflecting Ukraine's commitment to maintaining effective military communications amidst ongoing conflict.

Downs has faced challenges adjusting to Andy Reid's offense with limited practice. The Chiefs may utilize Downs primarily in short routes and third-down situations.
title: Chiefs debut: How much will Josh Downs play against the Falcons?

description: Sandeep Kumar, a 28-year-old police sub-inspector, died by suicide near Nagpur after being blackmailed. He had been in an extramarital relationship with a woman named Roli Gond from Sikandarpur. Kumar's wife has lodged a complaint leading to Gond's arrest for abetting the suicide. The police investigation revealed Kumar had a six-month-old child and was recently transferred to Pakri police station.

description: Siddhi Tandon established Cubs of Wall Street after noticing significant gaps in financial knowledge throughout her banking career. To-date, her nonprofit has empowered over 22,000 individuals via engaging workshops and community initiatives in various states. Her interactive teaching style simplifies complex financial topics for students. Moreover, Tandon authored a book designed to enlighten young minds about the basics of personal finance.
title: Student's first paycheck confusion sparks initiative reaching 22,000 people

author: PRANAV SHUKLA
description: Sanjay Manjrekar has weighed in on the celebrations of India's Under-19 cricket team following their thrilling victory in the Asia Cup final against Pakistan. With India clinching the match by just one wicket in a nail-biting finish, he remarked that the team should consider facing tougher opponents to truly reflect their competitive spirit. This opens up a dialogue about sportsmanship and the nature of post-victory celebrations.
title: 'Pakistan a soft target': Manjrekar questions India's aggressive celebrations

author: SAURABH SINHA
description: An IndiGo Airbus A320 encountered a landing gear malfunction shortly after departing from Pune. Prioritizing safety, the flight returned to Pune International Airport. After approximately two hours of holding to deplete fuel and assess the gear, the aircraft landed without incident. To ensure minimal disruption, IndiGo arranged an alternate flight for the passengers, reinforcing the airline's commitment to their safety and comfort in challenging situations.
title: IndiGo Guwahati-bound flight returns safely to Pune after landing gear fails to retract

author: SAHIL MALHOTRA
description: India’s batting lineup collapsed in New Zealand, as poor technique and questionable shot selection were exposed by testing conditions. No Indian batter scored 100 runs across the five-match ODI series; Virat Kohli’s 86 was the highest. Coach Gautam Gambhir warned the failures raise concerns for the ODI World Cup in South Africa next year.
title: A collective batting surrender! How the mighty fell in New Zealand

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Teray Boyd received a $28 million verdict following her child's traumatic birth experience, where brain damage resulted from the medical team's failure to execute an emergency C-section. The infant was delivered in dire condition, suffering from oxygen deprivation during labor. Inspired by her journey, Boyd founded two charities focused on assisting young mothers and children with disabilities, underscoring the vital importance of rigorous medical standards during childbirth.
title: Illinois family awarded $28m after son's birth leaves him with brain damage

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: Engineers have created a new solar panel design inspired by honeycomb structures found in beehives. This innovation addresses the issue of sunlight reflecting off flat panels at oblique angles. The three-dimensional design redirects light, enhancing capture potential by up to 142.3% compared to traditional panels. It could also adapt to applications beyond rooftops, such as vehicles and aerospace equipment.
title: How bees helped engineers fix solar panels' biggest flaw & capture more sunlight

author: HIJAM RAJU SINGH
description: Arshdeep Singh's exceptional performance played a pivotal role in India's 22-run triumph against New Zealand in the fifth ODI. He expressed gratitude for his fiancée's steadfast encouragement that both inspired and grounded him. The moment he proposed to her at Mount Maunganui beach stands out as nerve-wracking yet unforgettable. His standout bowling stats of 3/30 were crucial in defending a total of 209.

description: A Canadian woman traveled to Delhi on a tourist visa after establishing an online connection with a potential husband. Their meeting in Neemrana, Rajasthan, took a turn when the man hesitated about marriage upon discovering her age. This led to a conflict, prompting the intervention of local authorities after she reached out to the Canadian embassy.
title: Canadian woman, 61, reaches Rajasthan for marriage; man backs out over age difference

description: Tata Steel plans to finalize the merger of Neelachal Ispat Nigam Ltd (NINL) this financial year. The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) will review the proposed merger soon. Tata Steel has previously acquired NINL's assets for Rs 12,100 crore to enhance production capacity. The company aims to add 5 million tonnes of capacity at the facility located near Kalinganagar steel plant.
title: Tata Steel eyes NINL merger this fiscal; Rs 40,000 crore expansion awaits clearance

description: The Mumbai Suburban Commission has determined that a builder is obligated to refund a buyer's deposit, as the builder failed to provide adequate justification for withholding it. The buyer's request followed a denied home loan from banks. Despite the builder citing a non-refundable policy, the Commission found no compelling evidence to support forfeiture.
title: Mumbai builder ordered to refund flat booking amount with 9% interest

description: N Ramchander Rao expressed strong disapproval of Rahul Gandhi’s remarks on India’s democracy during the Bharat Summit, asserting that such comments discredit our democratic institutions. He noted Gandhi's role during the Emergency period and also criticized a foreign delegate's meddling in Indian affairs, calling it a threat to sovereignty. Rao suggested that external financial influences might be motivating Gandhi to stir unrest regarding the upcoming 2024 Lok Sabha elections.
title: Telangana BJP chief demands Rahul Gandhi's apology over democracy remarks

Gooptu's drag persona Zenia Fauxbia Darling merges Bollywood and queer culture, fostering dialogue in Kolkata. Venues like Kitty Su have supported this growth, hosting drag performances and creating a vibrant community. As drag continues to gain recognition, it becomes a significant part of India's cultural landscape.

description: The death of Dervishe Halil ignited a significant family dispute regarding a £1.1 million inheritance. Her will, established in 2018, notably left out her children Aysel and Attila. description: In a significant development, Saudi backed Yemeni forces have declared their withdrawal from the critical Bab el-Mandeb area, ceding control to the Houthis. This manoeuvre is aimed at bolstering security in Aden and surrounding areas. With the Houthis ramping up aggression towards southern regions, concerns have emerged over the impact on global shipping routes. The withdrawal follows a previously established truce that has now collapsed amidst renewed violence.

description: BJP MLA Shagun Parihar criticised J&K authorities over the alleged disrespectful handling of two slain Special Police Officers' bodies, claiming they were transported in a dumper truck. She questioned the delay in addressing their families' concerns, saying officials acted only after intervention from the Lieutenant Governor. The bodies of Rashpal Kumar, 45, and Bobby Chand, 57, were recovered from Kishtwar forests on Thursday, with bullet injuries, after they went missing on November 10.

The Rajasthan Anti-Terrorism Squad conducted extensive investigations, including analyzing call records and tracing leads.

description: A contentious legal feud unfolded between half-siblings Michael W Clark and Elisa Mrozinski regarding their late father's estate. description: Sundar Pichai congratulated SpaceX for achieving its first midair catch of a Starship spacecraft after its return. Starship had completed 14 laps around Earth and deployed advanced Starlink satellites during its flight. Despite the success, a first-stage booster explosion occurred shortly after liftoff during the tests.

description: Iran's deepening economic crisis has driven residents to advertise organs, including kidneys, bone marrow and liver, to pay debts and meet basic expenses. An Iran International investigation of over 600 Telegram listings found widespread multiple-organ offers, highlighting growing financial desperation. The crisis is worsening amid US sanctions, a naval blockade and regional conflict. Economists warn prolonged restrictions could severely affect oil revenues, inflation, public salaries and essential supplies, despite Tehran rejecting economic collapse concerns.

description: A clip showing world number two Sabalenka gesturing angrily and swearing in Russian during her 6-3, 3-6, 6-1 defeat to Svitolina was shared on social media on Saturday. Some commentators interpreted her remarks as an insult aimed at Svitolina or Ukrainians in general.
title: Belarusian Sabalenka apologises after swearing, denies targeting Ukrainian Svitolina

author: SHIVANGHI PAYAL
description: India and Egypt are looking to significantly boost their trade partnership through enhanced cooperation and investment. Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal highlighted the need for greater movement of goods and services. He mentioned that bilateral trade currently does not represent the potential of both economies. Goyal proposed creating a business guide to facilitate this collaboration. Both nations are focusing on opportunities that aim for mutual benefits in trade.
title: India-Egypt trade has 'sky's the limit' potential, says Goyal; eyes bigger investments

author: PRANJAL PANDEY
description: Iran's missile arsenal is estimated to consist of between 1,500 and 2,500 missiles, showcasing a significant military capacity. Both US and Israeli evaluations highlight Iran's resurgence in missile capabilities, despite previous airstrikes targeting production sites. Enhanced military strategies and precise targeting have allowed Iran to improve its striking effectiveness. The secretive nature of Iran's stockpiles and numerous producers complicate estimates, underscoring the necessity for vigilance among American and allied forces.
title: Iran has 1,500-2,500 missiles despite US claims of ‘decimated’ arsenal: Report

author: TOI DEFENCE DESK
description: China has expanded its PLAAF’s ‘three swordsmen’ fighter formation into four, adding the J-35A stealth fighter alongside the J-20, J-16 and J-10C. The development strengthens its network-centric warfare strategy, combining stealth, advanced sensors and firepower. China is now the second country, after the US, to operate two fifth-generation stealth fighters. The integrated formation also reflects growing competition with the US over sixth-generation combat aircraft technology and capabilities.

description: Aryan Deepak Jain found himself in legal trouble after being detained in Delhi for purportedly sharing altered photographs of Sonakshi Sinha. However, after being sent to Mumbai, a local magistrate released him, citing procedural errors during his arrest. The court pointed out that mandatory legal protections must be ensured for all arrests, as investigators aimed for a three-day custody to delve deeper into the case.

author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
description: In 2016, Mohammad Asgar Ali initiated his Chhath Puja observance during his mukhiya election campaign, vowing to celebrate the festival as a way to unite his community against religious divisiveness. Over the years, his family has wholeheartedly engaged in the rituals. This year, however, due to a family observance period, he will not partake in the rituals personally, but he plans to celebrate by enlisting a neighbor's help.
title: Bihar's Asgar Ali keeps 2016 vow, celebrates Chhath with family

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: A homeowner in Manhattan's Castle Village complex is involved in a legal battle regarding alleged water damage. The building claims the homeowner’s shower caused the damage, necessitating repairs at her expense. Multiple inspections failed to confirm the building's claims, leading to court decisions favoring both sides. Eventually, an appellate court ruled in favor of the building, requiring the homeowner to allow repairs.
title: 3-year shower-leak fight: NYC co-op seeks $170K in legal fees

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: During a house clearance in Massachusetts, over 1,100 fascinating pre-Hispanic archaeological items were rescued from a dumpster. Matthew Pioggia, noticing their historical significance, enlisted archaeologist Jeremy Pilver for help. Together with more than 40 high school students, they meticulously documented and cleaned these artifacts over nearly two years, unveiling their southeastern Mexican origins. In August 2026, the collection was respectfully returned to the Mexican Consulate in Boston.
title: Dumpster find saves 1,132 Mexican artefacts, students catalogue them

author: TRISHA MAHAJAN
description: Government agencies must now examine bids quoted over 30 percent below estimated costs to avoid quality issues. This new rule requires bidders to provide explanations for unusually low offers to assess viability. Agencies will still evaluate each case individually rather than automatically reject these bids. The finance ministry aims to enhance transparency and uniformity in the procurement process.

description: A woman held two health insurance policies - the first provided a sum insured of Rs 10 lakh against a premium of Rs 96,673. The second carried a sum insured of Rs 25 lakh and involved an additional premium of Rs 54,499. During her hospitalisation, a cashless claim request was submitted to the insurance company. The cashless request was not approved, with the reason communicated being insufficiency or non-submission of the requisite documents.

description: A Bengaluru liquor store charged a customer Rs 20 for a carry bag with its branding. The customer complained after paying for the bag needed to carry fragile beverages. The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission ruled against the store for unfair trade practices. Tonique was ordered to refund the charge and pay compensation for its deficiency in service.

author: YASHASVI VASISTHA
description: A serious bus accident occurred in Iran's western Ilam Province, claiming the lives of 12 individuals. The bus was carrying employees of a natural gas liquids company when it overturned on Saturday night. Six ambulances and rescue vehicles were deployed to provide medical assistance to the 16 injured passengers. Authorities warned that the death toll might increase due to some victims' critical conditions.
title: 12 killed, 16 injured as bus carrying oil and gas workers overturns in Iran

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: Elon Musk has signed the Stand with Jensen open letter urging the board to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO. Musk said many of Nvidia's critical supply chain deals were a handshake with Huang, not a written contract, and warned some could be lost without him. Huang resigned on November 12 after admitting an affair with Alice Huang, a suspected Chinese spy. CFO Colette Kress is now interim CEO.

author: VIVEK DUBEY
description: Karnataka minister Priyank Kharge said the law supported the state's proposed Mekedatu dam project, stressing that both Karnataka and Tamil Nadu must follow the Supreme Court's directions. The remarks came amid BJP accusations of Congress double standards over opposition to the project in Tamil Nadu. Karnataka maintains its right to build the reservoir to meet Bengaluru's drinking water needs and generate hydroelectric power, while protecting Tamil Nadu's Cauvery water share.

Witnesses noted that the man appeared to be extremely hungry and potentially mentally unstable. After being approached, the man fled the scene, but local residents provided him with food.

Overall, this ritual marks the beginning of the reading experience.

author: HADI KHAN
description: A Congress MLA, Harish Dhami, vandalised a stage at the Jauljibi Fair after being denied a speaking opportunity. This incident triggered a political uproar between the Congress and the BJP following the chief minister's attendance. Harish Dhami claimed he was not allowed to raise local issues, including a recent tragic incident. The BJP condemned his behavior and demanded an FIR against him for using abusive language.
title: Watch: Denied chance to address CM, Cong MLA creates ruckus on stage

author: YASHASVI VASISTHA
description: Global economic growth is projected at 2.8% in 2027, driven by declining energy prices and increased AI investments. Major economies like the United States and Japan are expected to surpass growth estimates. China's growth is forecasted at 4.5%, but domestic consumption issues may hinder progress. Risks such as geopolitical tensions and fiscal pressures remain significant concerns for global growth.
title: ‘Solid but unremarkable’: Goldman Sachs sees global GDP growth at 2.8% in 2027

author: PRANJAL PANDEY
description: Caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu reiterated his call for a national unity government. Gadi Eisenkot, his political rival, dismissed Netanyahu's appeal, viewing it as a strategy to create division. Eisenkot is currently negotiating to form his government, with a deadline of 28 days. Discussions are strained over the Knesset speaker election, with both sides presenting opposing candidates. Netanyahu's coalition proposal excludes Arab parties, complicating the negotiations ahead.
title: ‘These tricks don’t work on me’: Eisenkot rejects Netanyahu’s 'unity govt' appeal

author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
description: COSMOS-Mysuru Planetarium stands as India's pioneering LED dome planetarium, nestled in the University of Mysore campus. This remarkable facility boasts a 15-meter tilted LED dome, delivering stunning 8K-resolution visuals that promise immersive experiences. Focused on fostering curiosity in astronomy among youth, it offers interactive exhibits and training opportunities in multiple languages, thus enhancing its appeal to visitors and making it a significant addition to the attractions in Mysuru.
title: Why PM Modi called this new attraction in Mysuru 'a must-visit'

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
description: A remarkable archaeological find at Külhöyük has unveiled the oldest seed remains of 'love flower’, housed in a 4,000-year-old Hittite jug. The species, Centaurea tchihatcheffii, is currently endangered in Turkey, prompting immediate conservation initiatives. This discovery not only emphasizes the plant's ancient roots but also highlights the modern ecological challenges it faces amidst growing urban development and agricultural practices.
title: 4,000-year-old jug holds seeds of flower found nowhere else

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: In Oxford, Ohio, Bill Pyle's Halloween skeleton display became a beacon of hope for Tammy during her cancer journey. After receiving a touching letter, Pyle arranged the skeletons to honor her final radiation treatment, which shifted his perspective and deepened community bonds. This display is now a year-round fixture, updated weekly, with an annual homage to Tammy, illustrating how simple decorations can uplift during tough times.
title: Hated Halloween skeletons helped woman beat 19 days of radiation

title: Committed to ensure all inconsistencies in voter lists are addressed: EC to SC

author: SAHIL MALHOTRA
description: Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli endured a difficult ODI series in New Zealand, managing just 86 and 30 runs respectively. Despite Kohli's promising start, both struggled against the movement, bounce and relentless accuracy of the Kiwi pace attack. Their disappointing returns, coupled with India's misfiring top order, raise questions ahead of the 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa.
title: Kohli, Rohit miss the beat in their last dance on New Zealand soil

author: HADI KHAN
description: An 18-year-old woman named Shabnam was allegedly murdered inside a clothing showroom in Moti Nagar, Delhi. The suspect, reportedly a former friend, attacked her in a trial room using a sharp weapon. The incident occurred just before the store was to close for the day. Investigators suspect the motive may involve unrequited love and damaging personal relations between the two.
title: 18-year-old found murdered inside trial room in Delhi; suspect on the run

author: TOI CITY DESK
description: A man approached an electronics retailer in March 2024 to purchase a mobile phone through EMI. Despite paying for the phone, it was never delivered to him, though the EMIs continued. The retailer claimed he received the phone and sought police investigation against him for alleged wrongdoing. The consumer commission ruled in favor of the man due to lack of evidence from the retailer.
title: Hyderabad man pays EMI but gets no phone, gets Rs 1.14 lakh after consumer court order

author: YASHASVI VASISTHA
description: India's life insurance sector is expected to maintain healthy growth supported by increasing demand for protection products. Private life insurers are anticipated to see an annualised premium equivalent compound annual growth rate ranging from 13-18%. While APE growth and gross premium growth have been encouraging, operational challenges remain. Insurers are shifting towards more profitable products, enhancing their value of new business margins.
title: India's life insurance sector set for 13-18% annual growth in premiums through FY29

author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
description: In a candid social media post, a 21-year-old engineering student from Mumbai detailed her financial commitments. After two years of parental support, she assumed responsibility for her college fees, totaling Rs 2.73 lakh. Her monthly expenses consist of Rs 23,000 in rent to her parents and Rs 11,000 on groceries. Additionally, she prioritizes her future by investing Rs 40,000 in systematic plans, exemplifying the path to early financial independence.
title: Mumbai's 21-year-old spends Rs 3.25 lakh, pays own fees and invests Rs 40,000

author: SHIVANGHI PAYAL
description: Investors are questioning the sustainability of returns from heavy AI investments by US companies. This scrutiny may prompt fund managers to consider Indian equities as an attractive investment alternative. Recent data shows significant foreign investment inflows into Indian stocks after a selling period. Additionally, private-sector investment is on the rise, indicating a more dynamic market landscape. Overall, India is positioned favorably amidst shifting global investment trends.
title: AI losing its shine? Why global investors could turn to India for their next big bet

author: TRISHA MAHAJAN
description: Lalit Modi announced his acquisition of British citizenship at the Oxford Union in the UK. He celebrated this milestone with friends and family after residing there for years. Modi has faced allegations of financial irregularities since leaving India in 2010. He has consistently denied being a fugitive and claims to be available for investigation. Despite ongoing scrutiny, he expresses a desire to contribute to the country he now calls home.
title: 'My home for many years': Lalit Modi gets UK citizenship 16 years after leaving India

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: Jensen Huang, former CEO of Nvidia, sparked varied responses to his leadership approach and workplace interactions. Some employees advocated for his return, whereas many highlighted a pervasive culture of apprehension linked to his temper. Reports recount episodes of verbal outbursts aimed at senior staff during meetings and an overall abrasive demeanor. Recently, Huang resigned after acknowledging several affairs, one involving a suspected Chinese spy.
title: 'I hope you die': Jensen Huang told Indian-origin Nvidia VP during a meeting

author: PRANJAL PANDEY
description: An anonymous speechwriter for Prime Minister Andy Burnham was seen using ChatGPT to draft a keynote address. The speech focused on criticizing former Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher's legacy and addressing the cost-of-living crisis. Burnham emphasized the importance of these issues during his talk with Welsh Labour members. Opposition members have criticized both the aide's actions and Burnham’s government's plans to address economic challenges.
title: UK PM Burnham's speechwriter caught using ChatGPT to draft speech

author: SHIVANGHI PAYAL
description: Elon Musk has voiced his apprehensions regarding Nvidia's supply chain deals in the wake of Jensen Huang's recent resignation. He pointed out that numerous agreements stemmed from personal connections instead of solid contracts. Moreover, Musk highlighted a petition advocating for Huang's return as CEO, stressing his invaluable influence in shaping Nvidia.
title: 'Handshake' deals could fall: Musk flags risks for Nvidia after Jensen Huang's exit

author: YASHASVI VASISTHA
description: Protests occurred in over 30 cities across Portugal, reflecting increasing frustration over rising housing costs and insufficient incomes. Many protesters, including students and professionals, expressed concern about the affordability of housing. Demonstrators called for stronger tenant protections and limits on rent increases amidst growing inequality. The government promised to implement measures for affordable housing but acknowledged that changes will take time.
title: Tens of thousands protest across Portugal over soaring housing costs

author: SABI HUSSAIN
description: Ever since Usha’s name featured in the provisional electoral college for the Dec 5 IOA Executive Council (EC) elections, questions had been raised over how she could represent a sport with which she had no apparent administrative association.

description: Travis Kelce recalled watching mom Donna Kelce build her career during childhood visits to her workplace. From office cubicles to a corner office, her determination left a lasting impression and taught him valuable lessons about ambition and hard work.
title: Travis Kelce recalls Donna Kelce’s inspiring career journey while raising two sons

author: TRISHA MAHAJAN
description: US diesel prices have dropped below $6 per gallon for the first time in two months. This decline comes after prices surged to an all-time high in September due to global supply issues. Lower diesel prices are providing some relief to consumers, businesses, and farmers who have faced increased costs recently. Along with diesel prices, gasoline prices have also decreased, falling below $4 per gallon this month.
title: US diesel prices retreat, fall below $6 per gallon for first time in two months

author: YASHASVI VASISTHA
description: Kate Middleton will join Prince William in Mumbai for the 2026 Earthshot Prize awards event. This visit marks their first overseas engagement together since her cancer diagnosis in 2024. The awards will bring together notable personalities and focus on environmental challenges and innovation. Kate has been gradually returning to public life after her recovery, which has had its challenges.
title: Prince William, Kate to arrive in India in first joint overseas tour since 2022

author: PRANJAL PANDEY
description: In a recent Israeli airstrike, senior Hamas commander Samir Abu Younis was killed in the Mawasi area of Khan Younis, an incident that also left many injured. Known for his involvement in the planning of the deadly October 7 assault on Israel, his funeral is set for Sunday. The ongoing conflict continues to claim significant casualties on both sides since the ceasefire in October 2025.
title: Hamas confirms death of senior commander Samir Abu Younis in Israeli airstrike

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
description: Emperor Antoninus Pius, celebrated for his peace-driven rule and military expeditions, may have a newly discovered connection to history. A bronze leg unearthed in Scotland suggests a statue that honored him was disassembled by Roman forces prior to their withdrawal in AD 161, challenging prior beliefs of theft. This discovery sheds light on how Rome strategically managed its monuments, and further archaeological investigations could reveal more insights.
title: Mystery bronze leg in Scottish bog linked to giant Roman emperor statue

author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
description: An employee at Qualcomm found himself facing a layoff announcement mere days before stepping into marriage. Meanwhile, another employee publicized their severance details online as part of the widespread layoffs affecting the company. The restructuring led by CEO Cristiano Amon has left numerous employees in a state of uncertainty, accentuating the emotional and economic strains following these job losses.
title: Employee says manager confirmed layoff days before wedding

author: YASHASVI VASISTHA
description: Men gathered in the Swiss capital to protest against misogyny and violence directed at women. The demonstration called for men to take an active role in opposing misogynistic views, especially online. Organizers stressed the need for men to acknowledge their responsibility in challenging these attitudes. The event followed increased awareness of violence committed by men, highlighting the importance of addressing harmful masculinity.
title: Swiss men take to streets, call for stronger fight against violence against women

author: SHUBHANSHU DWIVEDI
description: New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner won the toss and elected to bowl in the fifth ODI.
title: After sitting out four games, Siraj gets his chance; Yash Thakur makes debut

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: A young baseball enthusiast from Seattle secured an esteemed baseball card during a Mariners game. This unique card showcased Jimothy, a raccoon who captured the internet's attention due to his extraordinary look. Initially a complimentary giveaway, the card has now emerged as a remarkable collectible valued at an astonishing $20,100. With multiple offers pouring in, her family decided to auction it on eBay, generating significant buzz.
title: 13-year-old finds rare free baseball card, sells it for $20,100

author: SHIVANGHI PAYAL
description: A significant setback in the US air traffic control communication system caused a grounding of flights lasting over four hours. This disruption was triggered by the upgrade of outdated equipment at a remote site coinciding with a spike in connection attempts, leading to sporadic communication and radar issues affecting several regional control centers across the nation.
title: How a glitch on ground triggered chaos in sky: How US flight chaos unfolded

author: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK
description: During a tense match against the Buffalo Bills, Patrick Mahomes vented his frustration over a controversial officiating call that negated a crucial touchdown. Ultimately, the Kansas City Chiefs fell short with a 20-17 defeat. Following the game, Mahomes expressed regret for his reaction, receiving a $50,000 fine from the NFL.
title: Patrick Mahomes fined $50,000 after Travis Kelce’s touchdown controversy

author: etimes.in
description: Ranbir Kapoor and Yash's 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' has achieved remarkable box office success in its second week. After recording Rs 72.90 cr net on Day 10, the film's total domestic collection reached Rs 685.60 cr. Its worldwide gross has surpassed Rs 1,200 cr, demonstrating strong international performance as well. The Hindi version has been the largest contributor, followed by Kannada and Telugu releases.
title: ‘Ramayana’ earns over three times as much as ‘Animal’, crosses Rs 1,200 crore worldwide.

author: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK
description: Cristiano Ronaldo expanded his Pestana CR7 hotel empire with a planned €60 million project in Paris, which was expected to open in 2027. The 210-room property was set to become the partnership's sixth hotel. With five existing properties across Funchal, Lisbon, Madrid, New York and Marrakech, the expansion highlighted how Ronaldo had built an international hospitality business beyond his football career.
title: Cristiano Ronaldo plans €60 million Paris hotel with 210 rooms by 2027

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
description: Cape May County has launched an ambitious restoration project aimed at revitalizing its local ecosystem. By focusing on rejuvenating tidal flow and creating new wildlife habitats, the area is already witnessing the return of various aquatic prey and bird species. The initiative also includes protective measures for freshwater ecosystems, promoting a balanced environment while enhancing public access with newly built trails and recreational facilities.
title: New Jersey's restored 290-acre marsh draws eagles, ospreys and herons

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: During a road trip to Georgia, Taylor Fritts showcased incredible presence of mind when his father suffered a stroke. While driving in Sweetwater, Tennessee, he observed his father's peculiar speech and actions. Without hesitation, Taylor contacted emergency services, leading to a swift hospital transfer via helicopter. His bravery earned him recognition as a 'Stroke Champion', highlighting the unbreakable bond between father and son.
title: 10-year-old calls 911 after dad suffers stroke behind wheel, helps save him

author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
description: The hooded pitohui, distinguished by its vibrant plumage, is the sole avian species known to harbor neurotoxins. These harmful compounds can inflict symptoms like irritation and numbness if applied to human skin. Studies suggest that these toxins are derived from its diet, especially from consuming specific beetles. Another species, the blue-capped ifrita, also possesses similar toxic traits. Caution is advised for birdwatchers in areas where these unique birds are found.
title: Meet the hooded pitohui, a poisonous bird whose touch can cause numbness

author: YASHASVI VASISTHA
description: More than 100,000 individuals participated in protests across France over the rising cost of living and educational funding. Demonstrators included members of the Yellow Vest movement, students, and various unions and activists. Although many protests were peaceful, some cities experienced clashes and police used tear gas. Key on the agenda was opposition to a proposed police law offering greater immunity for firearm use.
title: More than 100,000 protest across France for fifth consecutive weekend

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: In a recent custody case between John M Surma and Julie S Surma, a Pennsylvania court affirmed that the mother retains primary authority over extracurricular activities. The evidence presented indicated that the father imposed limitations on her involvement in various school events. John Surma expressed concerns that this ruling diminished his influence on his daughters.
title: Dad bars mom from school photo and tennis; Pennsylvania court backs her

author: SHUBHANSHU DWIVEDI
description: Supporters in the stands displayed a banner reading "Obrigado, capi7ão" — "Thank you, captain" — alongside images of Ronaldo lifting the European Championship and Nations League trophies.
title: Ronaldo tribute: All players wear No. 7, jersey immortalised with permanent change

author: YASHASVI VASISTHA
description: SpaceX's Starship spacecraft returned from its mission with a successful midair recovery by mechanical arms. The spacecraft completed 14 orbits while deploying 26 satellites before returning to Earth. However, the Super Heavy booster failed its recovery attempt shortly after launch, resulting in its destruction. The heat shield of the spacecraft performed well, indicating progress toward full reusability.
title: Watch: SpaceX's Starship completes first-ever midair catch on return from orbit

author: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK
description: Travis Kelce-backed Six Flags is facing mounting financial pressure, with nearly $5 billion in debt raising questions about its future. The amusement park giant is considering further asset sales after selling seven regional parks for $331.4 million. Industry analysts have raised the possibility of flagship destinations such as Cedar Point and Kings Island being sold, although Six Flags has not confirmed any specific sale plans.
title: Travis Kelce-backed Six Flags faces $5 billion debt crisis amid park sale fears

author: TNN
description: Dharmesh Naik, 50, and his wife Nimmi, 48, drowned after their boat capsized at Harangi backwaters. They were on vacation with their children and participating in water sports when the accident occurred. Despite wearing life jackets, both were trapped underwater during the incident. Police have registered a case against the boat operator for alleged negligence. Their bodies are being returned to Surat for the last rites planned for Sunday.
title: Surat architect, wife drown after boat capsize in Coorg
